case.case_title: Deshapriya v. Rukmani, Divisional Secretary, Dodangoda and Others
case.source_citation: Sri Lanka Law Reports [1999] 2 Sri LR 412

clause.text: All persons are equal before the law and are entitled to the equal protection of the law.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the suspension of the petitioner, a Samurdhi Niyamaka, without reason and on political grounds violated his right to equality and equal protection under Article 12(1) of the Constitution.
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioner claimed that his suspension was arbitrary, without any reason, and thus violated his fundamental right under Article 12(1).
case_context.respondent_argument: The respondents did not file objections or affidavits denying the petitioner's version; the 2nd respondent denied knowledge but admitted acting on orders from the Minister of Samurdhi.
key_facts: Petitioner was suspended without any stated reason.
Suspension followed petitioner's refusal to canvass for People's Alliance candidates as requested by the 3rd respondent.
3rd respondent instigated suspension by complaining to the Minister of Samurdhi.
2nd respondent directed suspension on Minister's orders; 1st respondent implemented suspension.
No evidence that 1st respondent knew the real reason for suspension.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: The court held that Article 12(1) guarantees equality before the law and equal protection, which prohibits arbitrary and capricious administrative actions without lawful reason.
reasoning.application_to_facts: The suspension was found to be arbitrary and without lawful reason, instigated for improper political motives, thus violating the petitioner's right to equality and equal protection under Article 12(1).
principles_established: Suspension without lawful reason violates Article 12(1).
Executive or administrative action must not be arbitrary or capricious.
Officials have a duty to refuse unlawful orders.

outcome.holding: The court held that the suspension infringed the petitioner's fundamental right under Article 12(1).
outcome.remedy_or_orders: The suspension was declared null and void; the petitioner is deemed to have continued in service without break and entitled to all arrears and benefits.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 12(1) was central to the court's reasoning as the suspension was arbitrary and violated the petitioner's right to equality and equal protection under the law.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The suspension was arbitrary and capricious, instigated by the 3rd respondent for political reasons, and the 2nd respondent should have refused to obey the unlawful order.
